title: Sum of Two Absolute Values Gives a Flat-Bottomed V
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graphing y = |x - 1| + |x + 1| produces a shape that is neither a single V nor a parabola: two steep arms rising from a horizontal segment. Write the function piecewise, and give its minimum value and range.

steps.title: Split the line at the two breaking points
steps.explanation: Each bar changes sign at its own zero, so the real line divides into three regions; on the middle region the variable terms cancel and only the constant 2 remains.
steps.why: Absolute values are handled by fixing the sign of each inside expression, which is exactly what the breaking points x = plus or minus 1 determine.

steps.title: Interpret geometrically
steps.explanation: A point between the two marked numbers has distances that always add to the separation 2, while a point outside must travel the separation plus twice the overshoot.
steps.why: The distance reading explains the flat bottom without algebra and predicts the slope 2 of each arm.

steps.title: State the minimum, range, and symmetry
steps.explanation: The function is even, so the graph mirrors across the y-axis, it never dips below 2, and every value above 2 is hit twice.
steps.why: A whole interval of minimizers rather than a single point is the distinctive feature, and it is what a smooth curve like a parabola could never do.

steps.title: Read the corners on screen
steps.explanation: In that frame the horizontal tread and both slope-plus-or-minus-2 arms are visible, with sharp bends at (-1, 2) and (1, 2) where the derivative jumps between 0 and plus or minus 2.
steps.why: Corners are points of non-differentiability, and a window that crops at x = plus or minus 1 would hide the change of slope that creates them.
